title: Tor vanishing passes from the restricted regular algebra to restricted free modules
statement: Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, $\rho:A\to B$ a ring map, $I$ any set, $M$ an $A$-module and $j\in\mathbf N$. If $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(B,M)=0$, then $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(B^{(I)},M)=0$, where both $B$ and the free $B$-module $B^{(I)}$ of finitely supported $B$-valued functions on $I$ are restricted along $\rho$, and Tor is derived in its first argument [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. No finiteness assumption is made.

source.place: Tag 066K, lemma-tor-amplitude-change-rings (free module in degree zero); Tor symmetry: Algebra Tag 00M3, lemma-tor-left-right. Sources read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066K and the TorSymmetry node.

proof.text: Prove preservation of exact colimits by short-complex homology using the equivalence between short complexes of diagrams and diagrams of short complexes. The colimit functor preserves homology by exactness, and evaluation does as well. Their homology comparison isomorphisms identify the homology of the colimit with the colimit of the homologies; homologyMap_mapNatTrans verifies compatibility with all cocone legs. Apply this to coproducts of modules, which are exact (Mathlib ModuleCat.AB). Evaluation at the three neighboring degrees transfers this preservation to chain-complex homology in any natural degree.

Choose a projective resolution P of the fixed test module M. Define the functor T taking N to the chain complex P tensor N, and module maps to the induced chain maps. T preserves coproducts because every degree is the tensorLeft functor on P_n, a left adjoint. Compose T with degree-j homology; by the preceding step this composite preserves coproducts. The projective-resolution computation isoLeftDerivedObj gives a natural isomorphism from Tor_j(M,-) to this composite; its naturality follows from leftDerived_app_eq. Transfer coproduct preservation through this isomorphism and the natural symmetry of Tor to obtain coproduct preservation of Tor_j(-,M).

Identify the free B-module with the direct sum of copies of B using finsuppLEquivDirectSum. The concrete direct-sum cofan is colimiting by ModuleCat.coproductCoconeIsColimit. Scalar restriction preserves coproducts, so its composite with Tor_j(-,M) sends this cofan to a colimiting cofan. Every object of this image diagram is zero by hTor. Its colimit is zero by IsColimit.isZero_pt. Transport this vanishing along the image of the free-module/direct-sum isomorphism. Empty and infinite index sets, degree zero, zero modules and zero rings are all covered by the same preservation statements.

lean.statement:
theorem free_restriction_tor_isZero
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (ρ : A →+* B)
    (I : Type u) (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) (j : ℕ)
    (hTor :
      IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).obj
        ((restrictScalars ρ).obj (of B B))).obj M)) :
    IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).obj
        ((restrictScalars ρ).obj ((free B).obj I))).obj M)
